chunks: And Ibn Abi 'Umayr and Safwan narrated from their men, he said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'God forbid that a good opinion be not held of the believer; and your breaking of his bones, whether alive or dead, is the same.'

key_terms.أَبَي اللَّهُ: God forbid / It is unacceptable to God
key_terms.يُظَنَّ: To be suspected / To have an opinion (zann)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of having a good opinion of a believer in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfahani’s al- Istibsar underscores the theological weight of husn al-zann (good opinion) as a divine preference, contrasting it with the severe penalty for violating a believer's physical sanctity. By equating the breaking of bones in life and death, the Imam establishes that the believer's bodily integrity retains its inviolable status even after the soul's departure, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding diyya (blood money).
